Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.description: Find live event push mechanism and hub
input.prompt:
In this repository, the server pushes live events to browsers (e.g. for a "memo" or notes-like feature). I need to find:
1. The exact mechanism used (WebSocket, Server-Sent Events (SSE), long polling, etc.)
2. The file path where the "hub" (the component that manages connected clients and broadcasts messages) is implemented
3. The names of the "memo" handler functions (e.g. create/update/delete memo handlers, or similar) that call into this hub to broadcast events to connected browsers

Please search the codebase (grep for terms like "hub", "broadcast", "sse", "websocket", "EventSource", "memo") and report back:
- mechanism used
- hub file path (with line numbers for key struct/functions)
- list of handler function names that broadcast through the hub, with their file paths

Keep the report concise and factual, citing file:line for everything.

- `SSEHub` struct (`sse_hub.go:56`) holds a `clients map[*SSEClient]struct{}` and a mutex.

- `SSEHub` struct (client registry, thread-safe via `sync.RWMutex`): lines 56-60
- `NewSSEHub()` constructor: lines 63-67
- `Subscribe(userID, role)` — registers a client: lines 71-86
- `Unsubscribe(c)` — removes a client: lines 89-96
- `Close()` — disconnects all clients: lines 99-110
- `Broadcast(event *SSEEvent)` — fans out an event to all subscribed clients, dropping for slow/full clients, filtered by `canReceive` (visibility/owner/admin check): lines 112-144
- Event types (`SSEEventType`) defined lines 11-21: `memo.created`, `memo.updated`, `memo.deleted`, `memo.comment.created`, `reaction.upserted`, `reaction.deleted`
- Wired to Echo route in `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:25-30` (`RegisterSSERoutes`) and stored on the service as `s.SSEHub` (declared in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:36`).

**3. Handler functions that call `s.SSEHub.Broadcast(...)`**

| Handler function | File:line (broadcast call) | Event |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:163` | `SSEEventMemoCreated` |
| `DeleteMemo` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:585` | `SSEEventMemoDeleted` |
| `UpdateMemo` (via shared helper `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`, called at `memo_service.go:513`) | `server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:71` | `SSEEventMemoUpdated` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` (via same helper, called at `memo_attachment_service.go:48`) | `memo_update_helpers.go:71` | `SSEEventMemoUpdated` |
| `SetMemoRelations` (via same helper, called at `memo_relation_service.go:48`) | `memo_update_helpers.go:71` | `SSEEventMemoUpdated` |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:126` | `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` |
| `UpsertMemoReaction` | `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:106` | `SSEEventReactionUpserted` |
| `DeleteMemoReaction` | `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:161` | `SSEEventReactionDeleted` |

Note: `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_update_helpers.go:66-83`) is a shared helper that centralizes the "broadcast memo updated" logic for the three callers above (`UpdateMemo`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations`), guarded by `isSSESuppressed(ctx)` (`memo_service.go:34`) to avoid double-broadcasting when a memo is created as a side effect of `CreateMemoComment`.</result>
